A_target.statement:
Let $T: \R^n \to \R^n$ be a [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linear transformation]].
Let $S \subseteq \R^n$ be a [[Definition:Measurable Set|measurable set]].
Then:
:$\map \lambda {\map T S} = \size {\det T} \map \lambda S$
where $\lambda$ denotes [[Definition:Lebesgue Measure|Lebesgue measure]].

B_source.statement:
Let $v_1, \ldots, v_n \in \R^n$.
Then the [[Definition:Determinant of Matrix|determinant]] $\det \begin {bmatrix} v_1 & \cdots & v_n \end {bmatrix}$ is the [[Definition:Signed Volume|signed volume]] of the [[Definition:Parallelepiped|parallelepiped]] spanned by $v_1, \ldots, v_n$.

substitutions.the unit square/cube: the region spanned by standard basis vectors
substitutions.image of the unit region under T: the parallelepiped spanned by T's columns

derived.det = volume of the column parallelepipe: T maps the unit region to a region of volume |det T|
derived.additivity/invariance of volume: the factor is the same for every region

object_map.reformulation: Reduce 'how does T scale a general region' to 'what volume does T assign to the unit region', which the determinant computes directly.

validity_conditions: T maps the unit cube to the parallelepiped spanned by its columns, whose signed volume is det T.
Volume scaling is uniform: any region can be approximated by unit-cube copies, each scaled by the same |det T|.
Absolute value handles orientation (sign of the determinant).
proof_plan:
Let $C = \closedint 0 1^n$ be the [[Definition:Unit Cube|unit cube]].
Then $\map T C$ is the [[Definition:Parallelepiped|parallelepiped]] spanned by the [[Definition:Column of Matrix|columns]] $T e_1, \ldots, T e_n$.

From the source result:
:$\map \lambda {\map T C} = \size {\det T}$

By [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linearity]], $T$ maps each translated and scaled cube $x + \epsilon C$ to $T x + \epsilon \, \map T C$, of volume $\size {\det T} \epsilon^n$.
Approximating $S$ by finite unions of such cubes and using [[Definition:Additive Function (Measure Theory)|additivity]] of $\lambda$, each piece is magnified by $\size {\det T}$.
